proof_nl: Let x be any real number and set m = floor(x). By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer, m <= x, and m is the greatest integer with this property. Suppose, for contradiction, that x >= m + 1. Then m + 1 is also an integer, and m + 1 <= x. This contradicts the maximality of m as the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Hence x < m + 1 = floor(x) + 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Using the defining maximality property of the floor function, any assumption that x is at least floor(x)+1 contradicts that floor(x) is the greatest integer <= x.
vetter_reason: The proof is a correct standard argument from the definition of floor: if m = floor(x), then m <= x and m+1 cannot be <= x, otherwise m would not be greatest. Therefore x < m+1 = floor(x)+1. The proof matches the lemma exactly and uses only allowed notions.
